sanskrit: rātriṃrātrim aprayāmaṃ bharanto 'śvāyeva tiṣṭhate ghāsam asmai | rāyaspoṣeṇa sam iṣā madanto mā te agne prativeśā riṣāma ||
english: Bringing night after night without weariness, as one sets fodder before a horse, may we, gladdened by abundance of wealth and food, never suffer harm from your neighboring fires, O Agni.

sanskrit: āgna āyūṃṣi pavasvā suvorjam iṣaṃ ca naḥ | āre bādhasva ducchunām ||
english: O Agni, purify our life-spans; bring us good strength, refreshment, and food; drive misfortune far away.

sanskrit: trīṇy āyūṃṣi tava jātavedas tisro vyuṣṭīr uṣasas te agne | tisras te tanvo devasaṃśitās tābhir naḥ pāhi sadam apramādam ||
english: Yours are three life-spans, O Jātavedas; three are the dawnings of your daybreaks, O Agni; three are your bodies sharpened by the gods — with those three protect us always, free from heedlessness.

sanskrit: pāhi no agna ekayā pāhi na uta dvitīyayā | pāhi gīrbhis tisṛbhir ūrjāṃpate pāhi catasṛbhir vaso ||
english: Guard us, O Agni, with the first; guard us also with the second; guard us with three hymns, O Lord of Strength; guard us with four, O bountiful one.

sanskrit: samīcī māhanī pātām āyuṣmatyā ṛco mā chitsi | tanūpāt sāmno vasuvidaṃ lokam anu carāṇi ||
english: May the two auspicious, mighty, life-giving ones guard us; do not sever the ṛc-verses; as guardian of the body through the Sāman may I traverse the world where wealth is found.

sanskrit: ya ṛte cid ity ekā ||
english: "Even without the rite" — this is the single (verse, cited by its opening words).

sanskrit: bhagehy arvāṅ upa mām iha tvaṃ mado nāmāsi mayi mādayāmum | surā ta ekam abhavaj janitram agner adhi jāto 'si brahmaṇā tejasā ca ||
english: Come hither toward me, O Bhaga; you here are named Intoxicating Joy — make that one exhilarated in me. Spirituous liquor became your sole birthplace; you were born from Agni, from sacred knowledge and from his brilliance.

sanskrit: sahānayā praviśehāntarā mām | viśanty ehi praviśanty ehy ā mā viśa pra mā viś- -opa tvā hvaya upa mā hvayasva | nariṣṭā nāma vā asi ||
english: Enter into me together with that which leads along. Come, enter! Come, enter! Enter into me, penetrate into me — I call upon you, call back upon me. For you are named Nariṣṭā (the harmless one).

sanskrit: yathāpaḥ pravatā yanti yathā māsā aharjaram | evā mā brahmacāriṇo dhātar ā yantu sarvadā ||
english: As waters flow downhill, as months pass day by day into old age, so, O Dhātar, may brahmacharins come to me always.

sanskrit: ā ganta mā riṣaṇyata prastotāro māpa sthāta sumanyavaḥ | dṛḍhāso amariṣṇavo māvapiṣyavaḥ ||
english: Come here, be not harmed, O praisers; do not stand apart, you of good intent; may you be steadfast, immortal, uncrumbling.

sanskrit: dhātā te hastam agrahīt savitā hastam agrahīt | mitras tvam asi dharmaṇ- -agnir ācāryas tava ||
english: Dhātar has grasped your hand, Savitṛ has grasped your hand; you are Mitra by your sacred law — Agni is your teacher.

sanskrit: agner brahmacāry asi mama brahmacāry asi | prajāpatiṣ ṭvā gopāyatu devāya tvā savitre pari dadāmi svasti caratād ihāsau ||
english: You are the chaste student of Agni; you are my chaste student. May Prajāpati protect you; I hand you over to the divine Savitṛ — may that one here move in well-being.

sanskrit: viśvam asi viśvapate sarvam asi sarvapate | taṃ tvāsau devāya tvā savitre pari dadāmi svasti caratān mayi ||
english: You are the All, O Lord of All; you are the Whole, O Lord of the Whole. You there — I hand you over to the divine Savitṛ; may he move in well-being in me.

sanskrit: samāvavartti viṣṭhito jigīṣur viśveṣāṃ kāmaś caratām ihāstu | viśvā dveṣāṃsi duritā hitv- -ā yantv anuvratā savitur daivyasya ||
english: Let the one who has returned, standing firm, desirous of victory — let the desire of all move here and be present. Having abandoned all enmities and misdeeds, may they go forth obedient to the divine Savitṛ.

sanskrit: ā no hasto akṛtāgāt svargaḥ punar aitu tanvā saṃvidānaḥ | prāṇena tejasā harasā balena mitro asmān varuṇa ubhayatas pātu ||
english: May the hand that has done no wrong, the heavenly one, come back again, meeting the body in accord. May Mitra guard us from both sides — by breath, by brilliance, by vigor, and by strength — and Varuṇa too.

sanskrit: yat kāma kāmayamānā idaṃ kṛṇmasi te haviḥ | tan naḥ sarvaṃ sam ṛdhyatām athaitasya haviṣo vīhi svāhā ||
english: O Desire, longing with desire, we make this oblation for you; may all of that prosper for us — now eat of this oblation: svāhā!

sanskrit: yad varco dyāvāpṛthivyor atho yad āñjana tvayi | tena sucakṣā varcasy ahaṃ bhūyāsam āñjana ||
english: Whatever brilliance belongs to heaven and earth, and whatever brilliance resides in you, O ointment — by that brilliance, sharp-sighted and radiant, may I become, O ointment.

sanskrit: yady aspṛṣi śliṣṭaṃ yadi vā svapnayānuśliṣṭam | āśliṣṭāvacchedanam asy abhidṛṣṭavīryam ||
english: Whether the clinging thing has touched one while awake or has clung while traveling in dream — you are the cutter-away of what clings, your power made manifest by the very seeing.

sanskrit: ava vār iva vārivā ava varṣaṃ girer iva | ava jyām iva dhanvano hṛdi śliṣṭaṃ chinadmi te ||
english: As water flows down, as rain flows down from a mountain, as the bowstring is cut from a bow — so I cut away what clings in your heart.

sanskrit: yat te hṛdi śliṣṭaṃ yac ca śliṣṭaṃ purītati | madhye pṛṣṭīnāṃ yac chliṣṭaṃ tat pārṣṇyāva chinadmi te ||
english: Whatever clings in your heart, and whatever clings in the peritoneum, whatever clings in the middle of the ribs — that I cut away from you with the heel-blade.

sanskrit: yat te śliṣṭaṃ kloma karṇeṣu yac ca śiśne sanābhyām | indras tad abravīd bhiṣak pārṣṇir āśliṣṭāvacchedanī ||
english: Whatever clings in your lungs, in your ears, and in your phallus together with the navel — Indra, the healer, declared: the heel-blade is the cutter-away of what clings.

sanskrit: eṣā vai duḥsahā nāma pārṣṇir āśliṣṭāvacchedanī | idam aham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasyāmuṣyāḥ putrasyāśliṣṭāṃ pra cchinadmi ||
english: This heel-blade, Duḥsahā by name, is the cutter-away of what clings. I now cut away the clinging thing from so-and-so, son of so-and-so's lineage, son of so-and-so.

sanskrit: vipaścit puccham ābharat tad viṣṇuḥ punar ābharat | tad agninā manasā saṃvidānaṃ pumāṃsam asyai putraṃ dhehi svāhā ||
english: The Wise One brought the tail; Viṣṇu brought it back again. That which is in accord with Agni and with the mind — grant a male child, a son, to her: svāhā!

sanskrit: vipaścit puccham ā bhara yarjjarahastā cittyā | yathāsyāḥ putro jāyatā abhibhūr ṇo vipaścitā ||
english: O Wise One, bring the tail with aging hand, with understanding — so that a son may be born to her, a conqueror, through the Wise One.

sanskrit: apehīto vipaścit tvaṃ pumān ayaṃ janiṣyate | pumān puṃso adhi saṃbhūtaḥ sa pumān eva jāyatām ||
english: Go away from here, O Wise One; this male will be born. A male, born from a male, arisen from a male — let him be born as male indeed.

sanskrit: bhadrāya karṇaḥ krośatu bhadrāyākṣi vi vepatām | parā duṣvapnyaṃ suva yad bhadraṃ tan na ā suva ||
english: May the ear cry out for good fortune; may the eye tremble for good fortune. Drive away the evil dream; whatever is auspicious, bring that to us.

sanskrit: akṣivepaṃ duṣvapnyam ārtiṃ puruṣareṣiṇīm | tad asmad aśvinā yuvam apriye prati muñcatam ||
english: The trembling of the eye, the evil dream, the affliction that injures men — that, O Aśvins, you two, release from us onto the unloved one.

sanskrit: yat pārśvād uraso me aṅgādaṅgād avavepate | aśvinā puṣkarasrajā tasmān naḥ pātam aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Whatever trembles in the side, in the chest, limb after limb of me — from that, O Aśvins garlanded with blue lotuses, protect us from distress.

sanskrit: yadīd amṛtakāmyāghaṃ (· ·) ripram upeyima | andhaśroṇa iva hīyatāṃ mā no nv āgād aghaṃ yataḥ ||
english: If through desire for immortality we have approached sin and impurity — let it be left behind like a blind lame man; let no evil come to us from wherever it may.

sanskrit: ariprā āpo apa ripram asmat | yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas tasmin duṣvapnyam ā sṛjāmi ||
english: O spotless waters, wash the impurity away from us. Whoever hates us and whomever we hate — upon that one I let loose the evil dream.

sanskrit: payo me kloma karṇeṣu payo me vīrudho dadhan | payo me sṛṣṭā deveṣu payo me dadhat ||
english: Milk-sap be in my lungs and ears; may the plants bestow milk-sap on me; milk-sap poured out among the gods — may it bestow milk-sap on me.
